The Specialist Pharmacist, as the subject matter expert, leads in their specialized area of pharmacy practice. In collaboration with teams and leaders, the pharmacist specialist will assist and be accountable for assisting the department of pharmacy in implementing departmental strategy, optimizing outcomes, achieving financial targets, and ensuring operational excellence. The pharmacist will serve as a liaison with external stakeholders to work towards achieving department goals. They will lead and/or coordinate team members to participate in internal and external committees, subcommittees, and taskforces/workgroups, which may include but not limited to UCOP and P&T. The pharmacist will help facilitate resident and/or student activities and learnings, as well as lead research and medication evaluations to align with overall departmental needs and goals. The Specialist Pharmacist will be accountable for promoting positive patient outcomes through incorporation of clinical practice, education, system thinking, leadership, and project management.
20% - Operational Excellence

Under the general direction of the Assistant Chief Pharmacy Officer for the Education Enterprise, this Pharmacist role serves as the recognized Pharmacy enterprise expert in pharmacy professional development, workforce development, learner training programs, and academic partnerships. This position applies advanced specialized expertise to provide consultation, develop standards and best practices, and leads highly complex initiatives that support educational excellence, workforce readiness, regulatory compliance, and optimal patient care outcomes across Pharmacy Services.
20% - Financial Stability

This role functions as the principal subject matter expert for pharmacy education and professional programs throughout the Pharmacy enterprise. Provides expert consultation to pharmacy leadership and interdisciplinary stakeholders regarding educational practices, competency development, accreditation requirements, learner programs, and workforce development initiatives. Leads high-impact projects and programmatic initiatives that influence educational outcomes, professional growth, and pharmacy workforce effectiveness throughout the organization.

In addition to administrative responsibilities, this position functions as a pharmacy educator, developing and delivering educational content to support staff competency, leadership development, clinical excellence, and organizational priorities. The role collaborates closely with pharmacy leadership, residency program leadership, schools and colleges of pharmacy, preceptors, and interdisciplinary stakeholders to advance educational excellence and workforce development. #CA-DS
Demonstrated scholarly achievements, including publications, presentations, educational research, or professional service activities
Ability to foster a culture of diversity, equity, and inclusion
Knowledge of pharmacy education principles, experiential learning, and learning theories

Ability to collaborate and work well in a multi-disciplinary team environment; including the ability to manage projects and deadlines, and to set and meet goals and priorities for self and others with minimal supervision

Problem-solving skills to independently recognize and define a problem, identify the resources available to help solve the problem, create and implement viable solutions, and follow through to ensure the problem is resolved to the satisfaction of all parties

Decision-making skills to independently exercise delegated authority to act, and to recognize when it is appropriate to seek assistance from others when limits of delegated authority have been reached
Ability to exercise discretion to ensure that patient confidentiality is maintained, and a professional, respectful clinic/department environment exists at all times
Working knowledge of federal and state or local regulations around medication handling requirement and controlled substance accountability
Strong verbal and written communication skills, interpersonal skills, and a sound work ethic
Excellent organizational, prioritization, and time-management skills
Ability to maintain composure, efficiency and a positive, customer-service oriented manner during periods of peak workload, with frequent interruptions, under tight deadlines
Ability to coach and mentor pharmacy residents, students, and staff
Advanced knowledge of pharmacy practice, pharmacy education, adult learning principles, accreditation standards, and workforce development methodologies
Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, and relationship-management skills
